products.name: Zapier AI
products.note: Workflow automation with AI; 7000+ app integrations; data flow governance; cross-app exposure

reading.body:
Zapier is a 13-year-old workflow automation platform that positions AI as a layer on top of plumbing connecting over 9,000 applications, handling the infrastructure that makes multi-app AI agents reliable at scale.

The company's two products sit at different points in the same stack. Zapier AI adds intelligence to existing workflows while managing data governance across 7,000 integrated apps. Zapier Central abstracts away the complexity of coordinating actions across those apps by packaging agentic behavior—lead qualification, ticket routing, autonomous task handling—into managed workflows. Both products delegate authentication, retries, and rate limiting to Zapier's runtime rather than forcing each AI system to solve those problems independently. This matters because AI agents at production scale fail less often when infrastructure handles the plumbing.

The data covers products and platform scope but does not address pricing, customer count, compute requirements, or the power and real estate footprint of Zapier's own infrastructure. It does not indicate whether Zapier's server infrastructure is cloud-hosted, on-premises, or hybrid. For understanding AI scaling constraints, what matters most is that Zapier sits downstream of compute—it optimizes what applications do with compute, not how much compute exists or where it runs.

profile_text.body:
Zapier is a for-profit startup founded in 2011 and operating remote-first. On its site it describes a unified orchestration platform for adding AI into a workflow, as an agent, or as a customer chatbot, connecting AI tools to the apps a business runs on and turning working setups into workflows that run without manual intervention. The site says Zapier offers 66,000+ triggers and actions across 9,000+ traditional apps, handling auth, retries, and rate limits, and that it works with tools including Claude, ChatGPT, and Cursor. It describes governance features for defining which LLM providers a team uses, detecting prompt attacks, toxicity, and PII, and routing AI through a company's own infrastructure. It also describes "Fluid Determinism," its approach to adjusting workflows as they run to reduce token use on repeatable steps.

The site lists two tracked products. Zapier AI is described as workflow automation with AI, with 7000+ app integrations, data flow governance, and cross-app exposure. Zapier Central is described as workflow automation with agentic actions. The site also describes Zapier MCP as a single governance layer across multiple AI tools, where IT sets rules once and every agent follows them, and says reliability is backed by Zapier's 13-year-old production infrastructure. It frames AI in customer service as giving customers fast answers rather than replacing human agents.

The held facts contain no lawsuits, no MCP registry entry, and no SEC or patent records for Zapier.
